title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Summarizing the market close on Friday, September 25, 2026

items.headline: US Stocks Close Higher, First Winning Week in Three
items.summary: U.S. equities ended broadly higher on Friday, capping their first winning week in the last three, as a cooldown in oil prices and easing Treasury yields provided relief. Despite earlier geopolitical concerns and a Fed rate hike during the week, Wall Street showed resilience, with technology and communication services sectors driving much of the positive movement.

items.headline: Akamai Technologies Surges on Anthropic Deal
items.summary: Akamai Technologies ($AKAM) surged 8.78% after announcing a seven-year, $11.6 billion cloud services commitment from AI company Anthropic.

items.headline: People Incorporated Jumps on Potential MGM Bid
items.summary: Digital media and holding company People Incorporated ($PPLI) jumped 8.9% following reports that MGM Resorts International (MGM) is weighing a potential takeover bid.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Rises on Analyst Upgrade
items.summary: Dell Technologies ($DELL) gained 5.08% after Morgan Stanley raised the odds of its bull-case price target for the company.

items.headline: Microsoft Leads Tech Gains
items.summary: Microsoft Corp ($MSFT) advanced 3.66% to close at $516.17, contributing to the tech sector's strong performance.

items.headline: Meta Platforms Declines
items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc ($META) declined 3.33% to close at $751.66, emerging as a notable loser among the S&P 500's top components.

items.headline: Twilio Falls on HSBC Downgrade
items.summary: Twilio ($TWLO) lost 4.41% after HSBC downgraded the cloud communications company to 'reduce' from 'hold'.

items.headline: Energy Stocks Slip Amid Lower Crude Prices
items.summary: Devon Energy ($DVN) dropped 3.78% as lower crude oil prices weighed on revenue expectations for energy producers.

items.headline: Tech and Communication Services Lead, Energy and Utilities Lag
items.summary: Information Technology led all sectors with a 0.99% gain, driven by semiconductor and AI-related names. Communication Services also saw strong performance, gaining 1.3%. In contrast, the Energy sector faced the largest drawdown, falling 0.88% due to lower crude prices and profit-taking. Utilities also lagged, losing 1%.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Data: Strong PMI, Low Jobless Claims, Shaky Consumer Sentiment
items.summary: Initial jobless claims fell to 197,000, nearing levels last seen in the late 1960s. U.S. new home sales jumped 6.4% in August, hitting the highest level since December 2025. S&P Global's flash composite PMI for September rose to 58.4, indicating the fastest output growth in over five years. However, the University of Michigan's final September consumer sentiment reading fell to a four-month low of 48.1.

items.headline: Fed Approves Bancorp Merger, Proposes Stablecoin Rules
items.summary: The Federal Reserve Board approved Peoples Bancorp Inc.'s application to merge with Citizens National Corporation. Additionally, the Fed proposed new rules for stablecoin issuers, requiring them to back stablecoins with high-quality, liquid assets and establishing an application process for banks. Markets are currently pricing in a 71% chance of an October rate hike by the Fed.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Kicks Off with Positive Surprises
items.summary: Early Q3 earnings reports for S&P 500 members show a 16.3% increase in earnings and 11% higher revenues year-over-year, with 66.7% beating both EPS and revenue estimates. Costco Wholesale ($COST) climbed 2.9% after reporting stronger-than-expected profits.

items.headline: Oil Prices Cool, Treasury Yields Ease Amid Geopolitical Watch
items.summary: Oil prices cooled on Friday, with Brent crude dropping 2.8% to $97.44 per barrel, easing market pressures. Treasury yields also pulled back, with the 10-year yield falling 5 basis points to 5.15% and the 30-year yield ticking lower to 5.49%. Geopolitical developments, including U.S.-Iran talks, continue to be a key watchpoint for market stability.
